    "scenario": "A logistics company runs nightly inventory audit exports from a SQLite database to a CSV with running balances per warehouse. The export tool supports checkpoint/resume for long-running jobs, but staff report that when they stop a run and resume it later, the resulting CSV differs from what a single uninterrupted run would produce. The tool must be fixed so a resumed export is identical to an uninterrupted one.",
    "environment_setup": "The Dockerfile builds a Python 3.12 image with /app as WORKDIR. setup_db.py creates /app/warehouse.db with ~217 transactions across 5 warehouses (ALPHA, BETA, CENTRAL, DELTA, GAMMA) over January 2024, with interleaved numeric IDs so the (warehouse_id, tx_date, id) sort order diverges significantly from numeric id order. setup_db.py is deleted after build. The main tool is /app/audit_export.py (~450 lines), a structured CLI tool with BalanceTracker, CheckpointManager, and AuditExporter classes. It reads transactions sorted by (warehouse_id, tx_date, id), computes running balances, writes CSV rows plus a summary section, and supports --checkpoint / --resume / --limit flags. A config.ini sets the batch size (default 25) and README.md documents usage and output format. Four bugs are planted, each in the interaction between components: (1) running balances are never included in the checkpoint JSON — CheckpointManager.save() persists last_id and batch_count but not the balance dict, and the resume path never restores balances into the tracker; BalanceTracker has no serialization helpers, so the agent must reason that balances are accumulated state requiring persistence; (2) the resume query filters by WHERE id > ? but the export sorts by (warehouse_id, tx_date, id), so records with lower ids that sort later are skipped and records with higher ids that sort earlier are duplicated — the WHERE clause is built in _build_query while the ORDER BY is applied separately in _fetch_rows, so each function reads as correct in isolation; (3) the CSV header write is guarded by self._header_written (an instance flag set after writing), and the summary is written at loop exit — on resume, a new exporter instance resets the flag to False, causing a duplicate header, and the old summary from the interrupted run is never removed before appending, causing a duplicate summary; each write path is internally consistent but neither accounts for pre-existing file content; (4) the export loop updates self.last_id only inside the batch-checkpoint block (every 25 records), so when --limit stops the loop at a non-batch record, the checkpoint saved at exit records the stale position from the last batch boundary, causing records between the batch boundary and the stop point to be reprocessed on resume.",
    "instruction_summary": "Fix /app/audit_export.py so that a resumed export produces exactly the same output as an uninterrupted export. The tool reads from /app/warehouse.db and writes a CSV to a specified --output path. With --checkpoint, it saves progress; with --resume, it continues from the last checkpoint. A resumed export must produce a CSV with the same header, the same transaction rows in the same order with the same running-balance values, and the same summary section as a full uninterrupted run. The invariant must hold regardless of when the export is interrupted and resumed. The README at /app/README.md documents the tool's interface and output format.",
    "solution_outline": [
      "Add last_warehouse_id, last_tx_date, last_id fields to CheckpointManager.save and the checkpoint JSON; update self.last_wh, self.last_date, self.last_id on every record in the export loop (not just at batch boundaries)",

      "Move self.last_wh/self.last_date/self.last_id updates outside the batch-save block so they track the current record on every iteration; save a checkpoint (with all fields including balances) just before writing the summary at the end of a full run, and also at the --limit break point"

    "why_not_textbook": "No well-known bug matches this pattern. The sort-order vs primary-key mismatch in the resume query is specific to this tool's design choice of grouping by warehouse. The missing-checkpoint-state pattern (balances not persisted) is not a famous library bug but a domain-specific omission. The _header_written instance flag that resets across re-instantiation is a common Python pattern that looks correct in isolation. The stale position variable (updated only at batch boundaries) is a subtle timing interaction, not a textbook off-by-one. None of these reproduce a named CVE, blog post, or textbook exercise.",
    "static_read": "Reading each function in isolation, everything looks reasonable: CheckpointManager.save() correctly persists the fields it receives; _build_query correctly filters by the id it's given; _fetch_rows correctly sorts by (warehouse_id, tx_date, id); _write_csv_header checks _header_written before writing; the batch-save block correctly saves a checkpoint every N records. The bugs only emerge when tracing data flow and object lifecycles: what state does the export accumulate (balances) vs what does the checkpoint capture (id, count)? The checkpoint captures an id; the export needs a (warehouse, date, id) tuple. The checkpoint omits balances; the export depends on them. The _header_written flag prevents duplicates within one run but not across runs. The position variable self.last_id is set inside the batch block; the exit-point code reads it assuming it's current. Each function is locally correct; the defects live in the seams between them.",
    "crux": "A checkpoint for a stateful, ordered export must capture every piece of accumulated state the export depends on (running balances) using a resume key aligned with the export's sort order (tuple comparison, not just primary key), must update that key on every record (not just at periodic batch saves), and must save the checkpoint at every exit point. File-level state (existing header, existing summary) must also be accounted for when resuming in append mode.",
    "challenge_kind": "resume_after_interruption",
    "sequence_invariant": "Regardless of when an export is stopped and resumed, the final output CSV must contain exactly the same header, transaction rows (in the same order with the same balance values), and summary section as an uninterrupted run from the same database.",
    "nameable_fix": "Persist full accumulated state and sort-order position at every exit point, align the resume query with the export sort order, and reconcile existing file content on resume",
    "self_check_blind_spot": "After fixing the resume query (fault 2), the agent re-runs with --limit 50 (a batch-aligned value) and diffs against a full run. The diff reveals wrong balances and a duplicate header (faults 1 and 3). After fixing those and re-testing with --limit 50, everything matches. The agent declares victory. But self.last_id was only moved into the checkpoint-save block's update logic, so at non-batch-aligned stops (limit=37) or after a full run, the position is still stale. The natural re-test at limit=50 (a nice round batch-aligned number) passes, hiding fault 4.",
    "reference_in_environment": "None. No .git history, backups, reference implementations, or project test files exist in the image. The BalanceTracker class has no serialization methods, so there is no code that already shows the correct handling of balance persistence. The README states the resume invariant but not how to achieve it. The config.ini sets the batch size but does not document its implications for checkpoint freshness.",
    "interaction": "The central defects arise from interactions between: (A) CheckpointManager, which persists a resume key (last_id) and batch count but not balances, and (B) AuditExporter, which processes records in (warehouse_id, tx_date, id) order and accumulates balances in a BalanceTracker — each component is internally consistent, but the checkpoint's coordinate system (id) differs from the exporter's sort order (warehouse_id, tx_date, id), and the checkpoint omits the exporter's accumulated state (balances). A third interaction: _write_csv_header's _header_written flag and the summary-write logic assume they are operating on a fresh file, but the resume path opens the file in append mode with pre-existing content; the new exporter instance has no memory of what the previous instance wrote. A fourth: self.last_id is updated inside the batch-save block and read by the exit-point save, creating a temporal mismatch when the tool stops between batch boundaries — the batch-save code is correct (save every N records) and the exit-point save is correct (save on exit), but they share a variable that is only current at batch boundaries."
